data.raw_text:
I just posted about “uncontrolled fields” not too long ago.

US airlines can, and do, fly into fields where the tower is closed or doesn’t exist, like what’s apparently happening here for about 5 hours.

Approach control works like normal, but instead of handing you off to Tower at about 5 miles out on final approach, you cancel Instrument Flight Rules (IFR), ATC gives you a last update of anyone they see on radar in that area & switches you to a “Common Traffic Advisory Frequency” (CTAF – it’s often the Tower frequency).

Then we just talk to each other & deconflict…it would sound something like this:

“Burbank traffic, Flight 1234, 5 mile Final, landing runway 28, Burbank”

“Burbank traffic, Flight 5678, we’re holding short of runway 28 for departure after flight 1234, Burbank”

“Burbank traffic, Flight 1234, we have taxied clear of runway 28, taxiing to the ramp, Burbank”

“Burbank traffic, Flight 5678, we are entering runway 28 for an immediate departure to the West, Burbank”

The harder part is departures, which we don’t usually do much of uncontrolled at a busy airport like Burbank. You need ATC departure clearance, which you get by calling approach when the local tower & “Clearance Delivery” is not available. They give you a clearance with a “void if not off (the ground) time”, usually about 5 to 10 minutes. That might be trickier here.

It’s not ideal, but it works, and it’s basic stuff we all did in Cessnas.

An uncontrolled field is not going to be capable of handling the normal volume of traffic at Burbank. Some reduction will be needed, but I don’t know how much.
